checks.detail: The prior lesson ends with the exact impulse-train sampling model, its 1/T_s-scaled replicas, and a forward reference to this lesson. This lesson should keep its single move at the acquisition boundary: when uniform samples determine a bandlimited continuous-time signal and when alias overlap destroys that guarantee.

mapping: x[n]=x_c(nT_s), with n dimensionless and T_s seconds
checks.guard: Keep capital Omega dimensional, lowercase omega dimensionless and periodic, and hertz f distinct from later DFT-bin frequency f_k.

checks.convention: Continuous-time analysis exp(-jOmega t), synthesis (1/(2pi)) integral X(jOmega)exp(jOmega t)dOmega.

checks.scale_guard: The 1/T_s factor belongs to the continuous-time replica formula; it must not be silently dropped or replaced with 1/(2pi).

checks.formula: Under X_c(f)=integral x_c(t)e^(-j2pi ft)dt, X_s(f)=f_s sum_k X_c(f-kf_s).
checks.guard: Do not mix this f_s scaling with the angular-frequency formula on one plot without declaring the transform convention and axis units.

checks.meaning: The sample sequence records normalized frequency modulo 2pi; it does not retain T_s or a unique analog-frequency representative by itself.

checks.identity: e^(j2pi(f+m f_s)n/f_s)=e^(j2pi f n/f_s) for every integer m and n
checks.apparent_signed_frequency: f_a=f-m f_s chosen in a declared Nyquist interval such as [-f_s/2,f_s/2).
checks.tie_guard: At +/-f_s/2 the half-open interval convention chooses one signed representative, but real-signal phase information can still be lost at that self-conjugate boundary.

checks.guard: The zero-phase 700/300 Hz example yields identical sequences, but an arbitrary phase is negated when the signed alias direction reverses. Do not generalize the zero-phase identity without this phase mapping.

checks.identity: cos(2pi 700 n/1000)=cos(1.4pi n)=cos(-0.6pi n)=cos(0.6pi n)=cos(2pi 300 n/1000)
checks.conclusion: The two stated zero-phase cosines produce exactly the same sequence. An analog anti-alias filter must act before sampling if only the 0-500 Hz representative is admissible.

checks.safe_statement: If an appropriate signal has X_c(jOmega)=0 outside |Omega|<=Omega_B and the uniform sampling rate satisfies Omega_s>2Omega_B, the complete infinite sample set uniquely determines the signal and ideal lowpass reconstruction recovers it.
hypotheses: bandlimited signal class and a suitable Fourier/L2 interpretation
the full ideal sample sequence, not a finite record
strict copy separation, or an explicit endpoint convention that removes boundary ambiguity

checks.condition: For symmetric lowpass support |Omega|<=Omega_B, adjacent replicas have a positive guard when Omega_s>2Omega_B.
checks.equality: At Omega_s=2Omega_B the closed supports touch. Equality is safe only under extra endpoint/phase conditions, for example when the boundary spectrum vanishes in the adopted signal class; it is not a phase-independent guarantee for sinusoids exactly at f_s/2.

checks.conclusion: Sampling exactly at the sinusoid's Nyquist rate cannot identify arbitrary amplitude and phase.

checks.frequency_response: H_r(jOmega)=T_s for |Omega|<pi/T_s and 0 outside, with the cutoff placed between the baseband support and first replica when a guard exists.
checks.reason_for_gain: The gain T_s cancels the sampled spectrum's 1/T_s replica scale.
checks.boundary_guard: State the value at |Omega|=pi/T_s only when an endpoint convention is needed; it cannot repair ambiguous Nyquist samples.

checks.units: The sinc argument is dimensionless; t and nT_s are seconds. The impulse-train reconstruction filter has gain T_s in frequency even though the interpolation kernel above has value one at zero.
checks.practical_guard: The exact formula uses infinitely many samples and a noncausal infinite-duration kernel. A truncated sinc is an approximation and must not be called ideal exact reconstruction.

checks.frequency_response: H_0(jOmega)=T_s e^(-jOmega T_s/2) sin(Omega T_s/2)/(Omega T_s/2)
effects: magnitude 2/pi at Omega=pi/T_s, about -3.922 dB relative to DC
spectral images remain and require an analog reconstruction/anti-image filter
checks.guard: A zero-order hold is not ideal sinc interpolation and does not by itself remove images.

checks.detail: The analog anti-alias filter precedes the sampler and suppresses content that would fold into the protected discrete band. Once arbitrary analog components sum into the same sample-sequence frequency, a digital LTI filter cannot infer their original identities without additional prior information or side information.

A realizable analog filter needs a passband edge, stopband edge, ripple, required attenuation, and a positive transition width. Oversampling can widen that transition, after which a sharp digital lowpass and decimation may finish the job; it does not eliminate the need for some analog rejection of energy that would alias into the protected band.

mapping: 900 Hz -> omega=0.45pi rad/sample -> +900 Hz signed representative
3100 Hz -> omega=1.55pi=-0.45pi modulo 2pi -> -900 Hz signed representative
checks.spectral_guard: For the real signal, each cosine has a conjugate pair. The positive 3100-Hz line maps to -900 Hz while its negative line maps to +900 Hz; 'opposite directions' refers to these signed complex components, not cancellation.

checks.formula: m=floor(f/f_s+1/2) away from negative/tie convention details, then f_a=f-mf_s in [-f_s/2,f_s/2); equivalently choose the nearest integer shift.
checks.real_tone_report: For a real cosine, report |f_a| plus the induced phase/direction change, not only the absolute apparent frequency.
checks.boundary: At half-integer f/f_s, declare which signed Nyquist endpoint is retained.

checks.detail: Sampling faster than a band's nominal center is not a sufficient anti-alias criterion. Ordinary lowpass acquisition depends on the highest occupied frequency; intentional bandpass sampling instead depends on both band edges, occupied bandwidth, spectral-zone placement, and out-of-band noise. Lyons sections 2.3-2.4 support this distinction.

checks.known: Desired support is 0-1.6 kHz; at f_s=4 kHz the Nyquist frequency is 2 kHz and the first analog frequencies that fold directly into the desired band begin at f_s-1.6=2.4 kHz.
checks.four_khz_option: An analog lowpass can use passband through 1.6 kHz and a declared stopband by 2.6 kHz if the stated interferer truly begins there, giving a 1.0-kHz transition; attenuation must be specified.
checks.eight_khz_option: Raising f_s to 8 kHz separates interference only if all significant unfiltered interference remains below 4 kHz or otherwise outside every alias band that maps into the desired 0-1.6 kHz region. The phrase 'above 2.6 kHz' alone supplies no upper bound and therefore no such guarantee.

checks.result: verified only at the theorem level
checks.detail: For an arbitrary real mixture whose occupied spectrum may reach 4 kHz, the phase-independent lowpass sampling guarantee requires f_s>8 kHz. At f_s=8 kHz, a 4-kHz cosine with phase pi/2 samples to zero. Over a continuous sample-rate choice there is an infimum of 8 kHz but no smallest strictly safe rate; a positive transition guard or discrete candidate grid is required to create a minimum.

The proposed eight-sample harmonic correlations are the next lesson's unscaled forward DFT values X[k]=sum_n x[n]e^(-j2pi kn/8). This exercise should not imply that eight samples reconstruct an arbitrary nonperiodic analog signal; it is a finite-coordinate handoff after the acquisition assumptions have already been fixed.

Oppenheim, MIT 6.003 Session 21, Osgood Chapter 5, and Lyons Chapter 2 directly support the planned core. Orfanidis sections 1.3-1.6 directly support the figure plan's alias map and ideal-versus-hold comparison but must be added explicitly if cited. Oppenheim sections 4.1-4.5 do not contain the brief's practical anti-alias/ZOH material; sections 4.8.1 and 4.8.4 do.

issues.detail: The brief assigns practical constraints to Oppenheim chapter 4 sections 4.1-4.5. Those sections cover ideal sampling/reconstruction and continuous/discrete processing, but the analog anti-alias transition and zero-order-hold D/A details used by this lesson are sections 4.8.1 and 4.8.4. Add those exact pointers.

The fourth figure explicitly cites Orfanidis section 1.6, but Orfanidis is absent from Sources to consult. Add Orfanidis sections 1.3-1.6 to the formal source list or remove the source-specific inspiration pointer.

'Nonoverlap is the reconstruction condition' is too broad alone. State uniform known T_s, a bandlimited signal class, the complete ideal sample sequence, a declared reconstruction band, and strict separation or zero endpoint content. Closed supports that only touch at +/-f_s/2 retain the phase-dependent equality failure highlighted by the lesson.

The figure plan calls for shifted sinc kernels without defining sinc. Freeze sinc(u)=sin(pi u)/(pi u), use the dimensionless argument (t-nT_s)/T_s, and distinguish the unit-height interpolation kernel from the ideal impulse-train reconstruction filter's frequency-domain gain T_s.

Exercise 4 asks learners to apply the nearest-integer-shift formula to 'three aliases' but supplies no three frequencies or sample rate. Provide the three numeric f values and f_s, and declare the half-open Nyquist interval/tie rule; for real cosines also request the phase or direction mapping.

'Interference above 2.6 kHz' has no upper bound. Raising f_s to 8 kHz prevents folding only for content adequately confined below its 4-kHz Nyquist frequency or outside all bands that alias into 0-1.6 kHz. The 4-kHz analog-filter option also needs passband ripple and stopband attenuation. Freeze interference support and a mask, for example pass through 1.6 kHz and stop from 2.6 kHz with a declared rejection.

AliasThresholdLab does not specify the mixture's exact tones, amplitudes, phases, duration/support, candidate sample rates, reconstruction algorithm, reference time grid, delay alignment, or the meaning of '-60 dB error' (peak, RMS, relative, per-tone, or aggregate). A known sparse mixture may also be identifiable below the ordinary bandlimited rate, so the demo must say it is testing ordinary lowpass reconstruction of an arbitrary 0-4 kHz band rather than model-based sparse recovery.

For a class that may contain a 4-kHz component with arbitrary phase, the safe theorem condition is f_s>8 kHz. Over continuous choices, 8 kHz is an infimum and equality can fail, so there is no lowest passing rate. Supply a finite candidate grid or a positive transition guard with explicit analog stopband attenuation; then the smallest grid value satisfying that contract is well-defined.
